Oh something I actually know a lot about. My organic professor had a massive hatred of triclosan and anti-bacterial soap. So the way that soap works is that the fatty acids on the soap comes off and binds to the bacteria. If you know things about biochemistry you will know that part of the molecule really likes being in water and part of it hates it. The carboxyl group hates being in water and the hydrocarbon chain likes being in water. So the part that hates being in water binds into the walls of the bacteria. The part that likes being in the water stays in the water. Now, when used with running water the fatty acids are so large and numerous on the bacteria that it yanks them off of your hands when the water passes. Think of it as if you are just standing in heavy wind, then someone comes up and hands your an open parachute.

What alcohol does is it goes it and just ripes things apart. What that O you see does is it binds to many biochemical structures. After it binds the structure no longer has the energy needed to repair itself because all of the energy used for wall creation is not readily there on the outside of the cell/bacteria/virus. That is why it is very hard for cells/bacteria/viruses to become resistant to alcohol based solutions, it is so small and violent. But because it is so small and violent it is not that harmful to humans because we are so big and mighty.

The reason that people do not like triclosan is because it tends to do something different. It goes into that bacteria and disrupts an enzyme known as ENR. The specifics are not that important to laypeople. Think of the bacteria as a factory. Triclosan runs inside of that factory and stabs the first person in a blue jumpsuit it finds. We know already that the worker in the blue jumpsuit is essential to that factory working. However, the factory is smart and instead of giving that individual a blue jumpsuit, gives him/her a green jumpsuit. Triclosan then runs inside and stabs no one because no one is wearing a blue jumpsuit now. Well, you might say, but Argi why not just stab any jumpsuit. That is the problem, if Triclosan just stabbed any old jumpsuit we could not use it because are own cells are filled with factories and people in a rainbow of different jumpsuits. That is how bacteria because resistant to antibiotics. We have given them so much of the complicated thing that it is able to change itself so that what we send inside cannot find anything to kill.
